newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu cuts short Europe visit - official.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu cuts short Europe visit - official.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will cut short a visit to Germany on Thursday because of Israeli-Palestinian clashes at home, his office said.
"They are returning home before evening," a spokeswoman in Jerusalem said. He had been planning to leave Germany for home late in the day.
Israel Radio said that because of the clashes, Netanyahu, on a three-day trip to Europe, would return some six hours earlier than planned, after meeting German Chancellor Helmut Kohl around 1000 GMT.
Eight Palestinians have been killed in two days of clashes with Israeli forces over Israeli policy in Jerusalem, holy to Moslems and Jews.
On Tuesday Israel opened a tunnel in the old walled city, which Palestinians said violated a religious and political status quo.

Netanyahu's spokesman made the announcement minutes after the right-wing prime minister ended a pilgrimage to the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp, where he chanted a Hebrew prayer for the dead at the memorial site.

Netanyahu has appealed to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to cool tensions and end the latest cycle of violence, the worst since the prime minister now in his 100th day of power took office last June.
